clue.text: Comic Louis wearing extremely meager support for the spine

indicators.note: something worn sits around its wearer, so the comic goes inside the other word

blocks.note: Louis C.K., the American stand-up comedian
superlative of bare, meaning as scanty as can be

explanation.surface: A stand-up comic in a skimpy outfit somehow tied to back support.
explanation.walkthrough: Louis C.K. is an American stand-up comedian known by his initials; 'extremely' looks like an intensifier but belongs to the superlative, as scanty as can be.
explanation.definitionFit: A backrest is the part of a seat that a sitter's back leans against, holding up the spine.

clue.text: Newlywed's second-rate car

blocks.note: slang for a car, as in a sweet ride

explanation.surface: A just-married person stuck with a mediocre automobile.
explanation.definitionFit: A bride is a woman on her wedding day or recently married.

clue.text: Gave Celsius over Fahrenheit, and got it wrong

blocks.note: preferring Celsius means being against the other scale, and con means against
F is the abbreviation for Fahrenheit
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: Someone gave a temperature in Celsius rather than Fahrenheit, a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Celsius over Fahrenheit' means choosing Celsius, being against (CON) F; it reads like a temperature conversion slip.
explanation.definitionFit: To confer is to bestow or grant, as an honour or title is formally given.

clue.text: Darned creep's bet won, overlooking the odds

indicators.note: skipping the odd-numbered positions leaves only the even ones

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on

explanation.surface: A detested wager that paid off against long odds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Darned' looks like a mild curse on the creep; it is the sewing sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Darning mends a hole with stitches, so a darned sock has been sewn again.

clue.text: For the most part, display colored vessel full of hydrogen? That's just a guess

indicators.note: most but not all of the word, so its final letter is dropped
something full of a thing holds it within, so the element's symbol goes inside

explanation.surface: Showing off a tinted airship full of hydrogen, merely a guess.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a hydrogen balloon, but the gas symbol goes inside the colour word, not the vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot in the dark is an idiom for a wild guess made without information.

clue.text: Much obliged, Eliot hugs Williams

indicators.note: to hug is to wrap the arms around, so the poet's initials enclose the other name

blocks.note: T. S. Eliot, the poet, by his initials

explanation.surface: A grateful nod to a poet embracing a fellow artist named Williams.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are spoken expressions of gratitude, said when someone has done the speaker a favour.

clue.text: Goth busted in stylish, small sneakers

indicators.note: something busted is broken apart, so its letters are rearranged
the jumbled word goes inside the outer words

blocks.note: S is the size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A goth arrested while wearing trendy little trainers.
explanation.walkthrough: HIP and S are joined, and the jumbled letters go between the I and P of HIP.
explanation.definitionFit: High-tops are sneakers that extend up over the ankle, a kind of athletic shoe.

clue.text: New York and half of London fused synthetic material

indicators.note: only half the city's name is kept, the first three letters

explanation.surface: Two cities merged into a man-made fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: A popular myth says NYLON was named from New York and London; the clue plays on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylon is a synthetic polymer, widely used as a man-made fibre for fabrics.

clue.text: Extra fee: sudden increase to limit burn

indicators.note: a limit encloses something, so the first word is put around the second

blocks.note: a surge is a sudden rise

explanation.surface: A surge pricing fee imposed to curb burning.
explanation.definitionFit: A surcharge is an additional charge added on top of the normal price.

clue.text: In Miami, one Scottish playwright

indicators.note: the answer is inside the run of words that follows, spanning their joins

blocks.note: read across the last letter of Miami, all of one and the start of Scottish

explanation.surface: A Scottish dramatist living in Florida.
explanation.walkthrough: Eugène IONESCO wrote absurdist plays such as Rhinoceros; 'Scottish' tempts a solver toward a Scot, but it only supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ionesco was a Romanian-French dramatist, a leading figure of the Theatre of the Absurd.

clue.text: Skillful catcher and pitcher rejected rule involving baseball windup

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the word for rule is read from its end
to involve is to take in, so the turned word holds a letter inside it
a windup is a conclusion, so only the final letter of the sport is kept

blocks.note: a pitcher is a jug for pouring
the final letter of the sport

explanation.surface: A baseball battery of catcher and pitcher who break the rules in a pitcher's windup.
explanation.walkthrough: In the surface, catcher and pitcher are baseball players; here 'pitcher' is a jug, and the skillful catcher is someone who catches thrown balls for a living.
explanation.definitionFit: A juggler throws and catches several objects at once, so this performer is a dexterous catcher.

clue.text: Simply enter uninvited, with gold for a politician

blocks.note: to intrude is to enter without welcome
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Advice to a politician: just barge in with money.
explanation.definitionFit: Justin Trudeau was Canada's Prime Minister, leader of the Liberal Party.

clue.text: Herb, in the mountains, wields each bit at least once

indicators.note: every letter of the word must be used, any of them more than once, so letters are picked and repeated freely

explanation.surface: A mountain herb somehow brandishing every piece of something.
explanation.walkthrough: An unusual device: EDELWEISS is built only from the letters W, I, E, L, D and S, each used at least once and some repeated, rather than a strict rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Edelweiss is a small white-flowered alpine plant, a herbaceous plant growing high in the Alps.

clue.text: Like J. & H., going after shelter

indicators.note: following something means coming behind it, so the letter is placed at the end

blocks.note: a tent is a simple shelter

explanation.surface: Two initialled people heading for cover.
explanation.walkthrough: J is the tenth letter of the alphabet. The pair 'J. & H.' looks like two people's initials, but only J belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: J occupies position number ten in the alphabet, so it is the tenth letter.

clue.text: Famous Amos doughnuts

blocks.note: first meaning: the famous singer-songwriter whose surname is Amos
second meaning: plural of torus, the mathematical ring shape

explanation.walkthrough: Famous Amos is a US cookie brand, so the clue reads like a snack menu; instead it is the singer Tori Amos and the geometric plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Tori Amos is the celebrated pianist; a torus is a ring-shaped solid, and tori is its Latin plural.

clue.text: Unfortunately, Ruth declaims around 500 times in a week

indicators.note: an unfortunate turn of events messes things up, so the name's letters are scrambled
the word for declaims goes around the numeral

explanation.surface: Ruth sadly makes a speech some five hundred times a week.
explanation.definitionFit: Thursdays are particular days that come around in each week.

clue.text: Saint Jack, notably, getting approval for a revealing pastime?

indicators.note: the notorious figure takes in the word of assent, which ends up inside him

blocks.note: Jack the Ripper, the Victorian London murderer

explanation.surface: A holy man named Jack gets permission for an indiscreet hobby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saint Jack' looks like one name (it is a Paul Theroux novel), but the saint and the Jack split apart; Jack the Ripper was the notorious Victorian London murderer.
explanation.definitionFit: In strip poker the losers shed clothing, so the game literally reveals the players.

clue.text: Inaccurately named creature — a kind of dog with protruding appendage — is below deck

indicators.note: in a down answer, below means placed after, so these pieces follow the knockout

blocks.note: to deck someone is to knock them out, a KO
an ear sticks out from the head

explanation.surface: A misnamed animal compared to a big-eared dog lurking below a ship's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deck' looks like a ship's floor, but it is the boxing verb, knock down.
explanation.definitionFit: The koala bear is a marsupial, not a bear at all, so its common name is a misnomer.

clue.text: Searching for fish: a serving of tuna-and-cod sashimi?

indicators.note: only a small portion of the word is served, its first letter

blocks.note: ling is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A sushi platter of tuna and cod for someone fishing.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'cod sashimi' becomes raw ling: ling is a cod relative eaten raw here.
explanation.definitionFit: Trawling is fishing by dragging a large net behind a boat.

clue.text: Foolishly unearth den below

indicators.note: acting foolishly means behaving without order, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone digging up an animal's lair from beneath, unwisely.
explanation.definitionFit: Underneath and below are synonyms, both meaning lower down than something.

clue.text: E's destiny

blocks.note: surface reading: what lies in store for someone known only by the initial E
setter's reading: the letter is printed heavy, a fat letter, and naming it that way spells out the word for destiny

explanation.walkthrough: The printed E in the clue is a typographic joke: a fat E, read as two words run together, gives the four-letter answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Fate is the power believed to fix events in advance, a synonym for destiny or lot.

clue.text: Say no to a thing

blocks.note: first meaning: to raise a protest against

explanation.walkthrough: The verb is stressed on its second syllable and the noun on its first, so the two senses even sound different.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to protest against; as a noun it is any material item.

clue.text: Power of misbehavior — that's gross

explanation.surface: Someone recoiling at how strong the pull of wrongdoing is.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinew means tendon, and by extension physical strength or force.

clue.text: Scandinavian bouquet contains roses, originally

indicators.note: a container holds something, so the word for bouquet goes around the letter
originally points to the beginning, so only the first letter of the flowers is used

blocks.note: a wine's bouquet is its nose

explanation.surface: A Nordic flower arrangement that includes some roses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bouquet' suggests flowers, which the roses encourage, but here it is the wine-taster's word for aroma.
explanation.definitionFit: Norse describes the medieval peoples and language of Scandinavia, especially Norway.

clue.text: Prefigure a silent cost

blocks.note: dumb means unable or unwilling to speak
a rate is a price or charge

explanation.surface: A hidden fee that foreshadows trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To adumbrate is to foreshadow or give an outline hint of something to come.

clue.text: Sneak taking off with artist's equipment

indicators.note: removing something takes it away, so the letter for with is dropped

blocks.note: a weasel is a sneaky person
W is the abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: A thief making off with a painter's gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking off with' reads as stealing, but W (with) is what is taken off.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is the frame that holds a painter's canvas while they work.

clue.text: Indisposed while traveling, risk CIA disruption

indicators.note: disruption throws things out of order, so the preceding letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A spy agency's operations risk upset for an ill traveller.
explanation.definitionFit: Airsick describes the nausea caused by the motion of an aircraft during a flight.

clue.text: Speaker's blnd?

indicators.note: what a speaker produces is heard, not read, so the description is taken by its sound

blocks.note: the word blind printed without its I is I-less

explanation.walkthrough: 'blnd' is blind with its I removed, so it is I-less; said out loud that is EYELESS, which also means blind.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking eyes means being unable to see, the plain sense of sightless.

clue.text: Winter conveyance made of pine surrounding large piece of ebony

indicators.note: to surround is to go all round, so the word for pine holds the others inside
only a piece is taken, here the opening letter of the dark wood

blocks.note: to pine is to long for, expressed by a sigh
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A wooden sled built from pine with an ebony trim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pine' and 'ebony' look like timber for building the vehicle; pine is in fact the verb to yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleigh is a sledge pulled over snow, typically by horses or reindeer.

clue.text: Harsh Russian region to the east of good German territory's western border?

indicators.note: in an across answer east is to the right, so the region is placed after the rest
the western edge of a written word is its first letter

blocks.note: the Ural is a mountain and river region of Russia

explanation.surface: A grim Russian area lies east of a fine German land's frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: A guttural sound is a throaty, rasping one, so it is harsh to the ear.
